children: What happened?

A number of stocks fell in the afternoon session after artificial intelligence and semiconductor stocks pulled back from the previous session's sharp rally, dragging down technology-heavy indexes. CNBC reported that the Nasdaq Composite fell 2.5% and the S&P 500 declined 1.2%, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average traded around the flatline. Nvidia shares dropped more than 7% after surging 31% in the previous session following Jensen Huang's return as CEO, while Anthropic shares fell 9%, breaking below its IPO price.

Tom Hulick, CEO of Strategy Asset Managers, told CNBC that Nvidia still has "a lot of things to worry about" regarding corporate governance. Mark Haefele, chief investment officer at UBS Global Wealth Management, said in a note that he expects greater differentiation between established platforms and companies dependent on debt, scarce capacity or continued speculative growth.

A pullback in artificial intelligence and semiconductor stocks can weigh on industrial companies that supply manufacturing equipment, electronic components or power systems for data centers. Share prices across a sector often decline together when investors reduce exposure to capital spending themes and turn more selective on growth.
The stock market overreacts to news, and big price drops can present good opportunities to buy high-quality stocks.
Among others, the following stocks were impacted:

Zooming in on nLIGHT

nLIGHT’s shares are extremely volatile and have had 69 moves greater than 5% over the last year. In that context, today’s move indicates the market considers this news meaningful but not something that would fundamentally change its perception of the business.

The previous big move we wrote about was 4 days ago when the stock dropped 13.9% on the news that AI-linked shares continued to pull back. Anthropic slid more than 10% following its debut, failing to revive confidence in the sector's spending boom.

Investors had looked to Anthropic's record $81.3 billion initial public offering and Nvidia's quarterly earnings beat under interim CEO Colette Kress to steady sentiment following Jensen Huang's resignation, CNBC reported.

Instead, Anthropic's retreat toward its $83 offer price echoed Seaport Research warnings, covered by CNBC, that its valuation demands much faster revenue growth. Separately, Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook warned against delaying rate hikes ahead of an expected December increase. Compounding the concerns, President Donald Trump threatened penalties on overseas U.S. data-center builds as new Commerce Department export-licensing rules weighed on chipmakers.

nLIGHT is down 13.9% since the beginning of the year, and at $33.05 per share, it is trading 61.1% below its 52-week high of $84.95 from May 2026. Despite the year-to-date decline, investors who bought $1,000 worth of nLIGHT’s shares 5 years ago would now be looking at an investment worth $1,264.
